title: TAMBO: A Novel Neutrino Telescope for High-Energy Astrophysical Neutrino Detection
summary: The detection of astrophysical neutrino point sources remains challenging due to atmospheric backgrounds obscuring signal and statistical penalties from the look-elsewhere effect. The Tau Air-shower Mountain-Based Observatory (TAMBO) is a neutrino telescope that achieves unprecedented signal-to-background discrimination in the 1-1000 PeV energy range. Leveraging its unique deep valley geometry, TAMBO will generate an exceptionally pure neutrino sample, enabling precise investigations of neutrino sources. Preliminary sensitivity studies demonstrate TAMBO's potential to map diffuse and point-source neutrino emissions, representing a significant advancement in high-energy neutrino astronomy.

AI.tldr: TAMBO is a neutrino telescope with a unique deep valley geometry that enables unprecedented signal-to-background discrimination in the 1-1000 PeV range, allowing precise mapping of diffuse and point-source neutrino emissions.
AI.motivation: The detection of astrophysical neutrino point sources is challenging due to atmospheric backgrounds and the look-elsewhere effect, motivating the need for a telescope with better signal-to-background discrimination.
AI.method: TAMBO leverages its unique deep valley geometry to generate an exceptionally pure neutrino sample with unprecedented signal-to-background discrimination in the 1-1000 PeV energy range.
AI.result: Preliminary sensitivity studies demonstrate TAMBO's potential to map diffuse and point-source neutrino emissions.
AI.conclusion: TAMBO represents a significant advancement in high-energy neutrino astronomy by enabling precise investigations of neutrino sources.

title: A synchro-curvature treatment of gamma-ray luminosity trends in pulsars
comment: Accepted for Publication in the Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
summary: In recent years, the Large Area Telescope (LAT) onboard the \emph{Fermi} satellite has detected more than 300 pulsars in the high energy range. The population studies of high energy pulsars show that the gamma ray luminosity of a pulsar ($L_γ$) can be expressed in terms of the spin down luminosity ($\dot{E}$) as $L_γ\propto \dot {E}^s$ having exponent $s\sim 0.68$. This high energy emission, assumed to originate far from the stellar surface and near the light cylinder, is usually studied in either purely curvature or purely synchrotron regime. In this work, we adopt a synchro-curvature radiation framework to understand the origin of gamma ray emission from the pulsar and its implications at the population-level. By comparing the observed cutoff energies of the differential gamma-ray spectra with the theoretical synchro-curvature predictions and enforcing radiation reaction approximation, we determine the equilibrium Lorentz factor and pitch angle of the emitting charged particles. This approach allows to quantify the relative roles of curvature and synchrotron radiation to the radiative losses, thereby providing a physically grounded interpretation of the luminosity trend across the pulsar population.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a synchro-curvature radiation framework to explain gamma-ray emission from Fermi-LAT pulsars, determining equilibrium Lorentz factors and pitch angles via cutoff energy comparisons, and providing a physical basis for the observed L_γ ∝ \dot{E}^0.68 luminosity scaling across the pulsar population.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of gamma-ray emission from pulsars detected by Fermi-LAT and explain the observed population-level luminosity trend L_γ ∝ \dot{E}^0.68 using a physically grounded radiation framework.
AI.method: Adopts a synchro-curvature radiation framework (combining curvature and synchrotron regimes), compares observed cutoff energies of differential gamma-ray spectra with theoretical predictions, and enforces radiation reaction approximation to determine equilibrium Lorentz factor and pitch angle of emitting charged particles.
AI.result: Determines equilibrium Lorentz factor and pitch angle of emitting particles; quantifies relative contributions of curvature and synchrotron radiation to radiative losses; provides a physically grounded interpretation of the L_γ ∝ \dot{E}^0.68 luminosity trend.
AI.conclusion: The synchro-curvature framework successfully explains the gamma-ray emission origin from pulsars and the observed luminosity scaling relation across the population, bridging curvature and synchrotron regimes.

title: A phase-coherent timing solution for the X-ray dim isolated neutron star eRASSU J131716.9-402647
comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Based on its predominantly thermal X-ray emission and long spin period, the isolated neutron star eRASSU J131716.9-402647 is one of the most promising candidates for membership in the still small class of X-ray dim isolated neutron stars (XDINSs). Confirmation of this classification, however, requires a more detailed characterisation of the source's timing and spectral properties. In this work, we present new NICER observations which, together with previous X-ray follow-up, allow us to constrain the timing properties and long-term evolution of eRASSU J131716.9-402647. We obtain a coherent timing solution with a spin period of $P\sim12.8$ s and a period derivative of $\dot{P}\sim9\times 10^{-14}$ s s$^{-1}$, which best-describes the spin evolution of the source. These parameters imply a dipolar magnetic field strength of $3\times10^{13}$ G and a spin-down luminosity of order $10^{30}$ erg s$^{-1}$. Spectral modelling reveals no significant change in the spectral state over the 15 months of observational monitoring and indicates a thermal luminosity that likely exceeds the rotational energy loss. This suggests a thermal evolution that has been significantly influenced by past reheating. The energy dependence of the double-humped pulse profile closely resembles that observed in the XDINS RX J1308.6+2127, with the pulsed fraction increasing towards higher energies. Taken together, these results unambiguously confirm the XDINS nature of eRASSU J131716.9-402647, making it the first newly confirmed XDINS in more than two decades.

AI.tldr: Using NICER observations and previous X-ray data, the study confirms eRASSU J131716.9-402647 as an X-ray dim isolated neutron star (XDINS) — the first newly confirmed member of this class in over 20 years — with a spin period of ~12.8 s, period derivative of ~9×10⁻¹⁴ s s⁻¹, dipolar magnetic field of ~3×10¹³ G, and thermal luminosity exceeding spin-down power, indicating past reheating.
AI.motivation: eRASSU J131716.9-402647 was a promising XDINS candidate based on its thermal X-ray emission and long spin period, but confirmation required detailed timing and spectral characterization, which had not been done.
AI.method: New NICER observations were combined with previous X-ray follow-up data to derive a coherent timing solution, measure spin period and period derivative, model spectra, and analyze pulse profile energy dependence over 15 months.
AI.result: A coherent timing solution yields P~12.8 s, Ṗ~9×10⁻¹⁴ s s⁻¹, B~3×10¹³ G, spin-down luminosity ~10³⁰ erg s⁻¹. No significant spectral change over 15 months; thermal luminosity exceeds rotational energy loss. Double-humped pulse profile shows increasing pulsed fraction with energy, similar to XDINS RX J1308.6+2127.
AI.conclusion: The results unambiguously confirm eRASSU J131716.9-402647 as an XDINS, making it the first newly confirmed member of this class in over two decades, with evidence of past reheating influencing its thermal evolution.

title: Intermediate States in Chaotic Triple Evolution and Applications to Black Hole Merger Statistics
summary: Three-body interactions exhibit phases of strong chaotic evolution as well as hierarchical motion where one body separates from a binary and follows a hyperbolic or elliptic trajectory around it. The binaries produced during phases of hierarchical motion may lead to gravitational wave (GW) inspirals, but this depends on the outcomes of the chaotic states. In this paper we re-derive the elliptic outcome distribution using equilibrium statistical mechanics and explore it together with the hyperbolic distribution. When comparing to N-body simulations, we find that we can reduce the elliptic outcome model to one free parameter instead of the previously used two and that the predicted disintegration probabilities agree except for very low angular momentum triples. We then use both outcome distributions along with a star cluster model to design a Monte Carlo algorithm for repeated binary-single scatterings within dense star systems. We explore star cluster masses of $[10^5 - 10^7] M_{\odot}$, with the goal of quantifying observably eccentric merger (OEM) GWs, visible to instruments such as LIGO and Virgo. Assuming an OEM detection sensitivity of $f_{\rm min}=10 {\rm Hz}, e_{\rm min} = 0.1$, we find the elliptic OEMs are about $\sim (32 - 63)\%$ of the total elliptic mergers and that the total cluster mass greatly impacts the fraction of ejected binaries. The OEM to total merger fraction (OEM fraction) is found to be $(2.6 - 4.4)\%$. Considering the detection sensitivity that GW interferometers have today $(f_{\rm min} \simeq 34.4 {\rm Hz})$ we obtain the OEM fraction in the $(1.6 - 3.1)\%$ range.

AI.tldr: The paper derives elliptic outcome distributions for three-body interactions using statistical mechanics, reduces a model to one free parameter, and develops a Monte Carlo algorithm to simulate repeated binary-single scatterings in dense star clusters. It finds that elliptic observable eccentric mergers (OEMs) constitute ~32-63% of elliptic mergers, and the total OEM fraction is ~2.6-4.4% (or 1.6-3.1% at current LIGO/Virgo sensitivity).
AI.motivation: To quantify the production of observably eccentric gravitational wave mergers (OEMs) from three-body interactions in dense star clusters, and to improve theoretical models of elliptic outcome distributions.
AI.method: Equilibrium statistical mechanics re-derivation of the elliptic outcome distribution; reduction to one free parameter; comparison with N-body simulations; Monte Carlo algorithm for repeated binary-single scatterings in star cluster models with masses 10^5–10^7 M⊙.
AI.result: Elliptic OEMs are ~32–63% of elliptic mergers; total OEM fraction is 2.6–4.4% (at f_min=10 Hz, e_min=0.1) or 1.6–3.1% (at current LIGO/Virgo sensitivity ~34.4 Hz). Cluster mass strongly affects ejected binary fraction.
AI.conclusion: The elliptic outcome model is simplified to one free parameter and agrees with N-body simulations except at very low angular momenta. The OEM fraction is modest but non-negligible, and detectable with current and upcoming GW interferometers.

title: pop-cosmos: Disentangling galaxy properties from observables using data-driven approaches
summary: The physical processes that shape a galaxy's spectrum are strongly degenerate in observations, obscuring which processes act independently. Leveraging the pop-cosmos generative galaxy population model, we investigate how many independent degrees of freedom the rest-frame optical SED contains. We use a $β$-variational autoencoder (VAE) to compress a 16-parameter stellar population synthesis (SPS) description into a disentangled latent representation interpreted through mutual information (MI). We find that five independent dimensions suffice, corresponding to stellar mass, recent star formation, dust, and two -- not the three or four assumed by standard nebular models -- degrees of freedom in the ionization state of the gas. Stellar metallicity and stellar age are not among these primary drivers; their spectral effects are distributed across the others rather than independently encoded. By tying each dimension to specific spectral features, this decomposition breaks the star-formation--dust--metallicity degeneracies that limit broadband photometry, and recovers the physical conditions of the gas more cleanly than the line-ratio diagnostics in standard use.

AI.tldr: Using a β-VAE on the pop-cosmos model, the authors find that the rest-frame optical SED of galaxies can be described by five independent physical dimensions: stellar mass, recent star formation, dust, and two (not three or four) ionization state degrees of freedom. Stellar metallicity and age are not independent but distributed across other factors.
AI.motivation: To break degeneracies in galaxy spectra and identify how many truly independent physical processes shape the rest-frame optical SED, as opposed to the strongly degenerate interpretations from observations.
AI.method: Applied a β-VAE to compress a 16-parameter SPS description into a disentangled latent space, quantified using mutual information (MI).
AI.result: Five independent dimensions suffice: stellar mass, recent star formation, dust, and two ionization state degrees of freedom. Stellar metallicity and age are not independent but distributed across other factors.
AI.conclusion: This decomposition breaks star-formation–dust–metallicity degeneracies limiting broadband photometry and recovers gas physical conditions more cleanly than standard line-ratio diagnostics.

title: A magnetar formation in binary neutron star merger
summary: We conduct a global general relativistic neutrino-radiation-transfer magnetohydrodynamics simulation of a $1.35$-$1.35M_\odot$ binary neutron star with the unprecedented spatial resolution of $6.25$\,m on the Japanese supercomputer FUGAKU. The total consumed CPU time is $\approx 530$ million core hours. We initialize the binary neutron star's magnetic field to be $3.16\times 10^{12}$~G at maximum, which is compatible with the upper end of the observed binary pulsars. We demonstrate that the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability that emerges when the two neutron stars touch amplifies the magnetic field to an expected electromagnetic saturation energy of $\sim 10^{50}$~erg within $3$~ms after the merger. The spectral analysis indicates that the Kazantsev and Kolmogorov spectra are reproduced in the magnetic and kinetic power spectral densities, respectively. We also find that it induces stellar-scale magnetic field amplification by at least a factor of $316$. We conclude that a magnetar may form at least temporarily following neutron star mergers in a few ms.

AI.tldr: A high-resolution (6.25 m) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics simulation on the FUGAKU supercomputer shows that Kelvin-Helmholtz instability in merging binary neutron stars amplifies magnetic fields to ~10⁵⁰ erg within 3 ms, producing Kazantsev/Kolmogorov spectra and stellar-scale amplification by >316×, suggesting magnetar formation within a few ms post-merger.
AI.motivation: To understand the magnetic field amplification mechanism and timescale during binary neutron star mergers, and to assess whether magnetar formation is possible immediately after merger, using unprecedented spatial resolution to capture small-scale instabilities.
AI.method: Global general relativistic neutrino-radiation-transfer magnetohydrodynamics simulation of a 1.35-1.35 M⊙ binary neutron star at 6.25 m resolution on the FUGAKU supercomputer, with an initial magnetic field of 3.16×10¹² G (consistent with observed binary pulsars). Total CPU time ≈ 530 million core hours.
AI.result: Kelvin-Helmholtz instability amplifies the magnetic field to an electromagnetic saturation energy of ~10⁵⁰ erg within 3 ms post-merger. Magnetic and kinetic power spectral densities follow Kazantsev and Kolmogorov spectra, respectively. Stellar-scale magnetic field amplification by at least a factor of 316 is observed.
AI.conclusion: A magnetar may form at least temporarily within a few ms following neutron star mergers.

title: Comparison and verification methods to trace interaction-driven disturbances in galaxies
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 17 pages
summary: Low surface brightness tidal debris around galaxies, such as tails, streams, and shells, together with other interaction-driven morphological disturbances, serve as valuable indicators of past or ongoing galaxy mergers. With the growing data volume from surveys like the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), automated detection methods are essential. This paper evaluates the performance of two automated methods, a Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) model and the Concentration-Asymmetry-Smoothness (CAS) parameter method, in tracing interaction-driven disturbances and merger signatures, with visual classification used as the benchmark. Visual classification yields a high-confidence disturbance fraction of 25.1 +/- 1.5% in our sample and serves as the reference standard for assessing the completeness and precision of the automated approaches. Visual classification is affected by galaxy distance and image resolution, which limit the detectability of faint low surface brightness structures. The SSL model achieves high recall (0.86 +/- 0.04) and low contamination (0.2) by retraining only its linear classifier on a small labelled dataset, making it suitable for identifying a broad set of disturbed systems, including faint tidal debris and other interaction-driven morphological disturbances, thereby providing a more complete census of merger-related features. The CAS method, using the traditional threshold A > 0.35, shows higher precision (0.77) but lower recall (0.20), indicating a conservative approach that captures cleaner but less complete samples. Visual classification and the SSL model show a significant positive correlation between stellar mass and disturbance fraction, while the CAS method exhibits a much weaker trend.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates two automated methods (SSL model and CAS parameters) for detecting merger-induced tidal debris in galaxies, using visual classification as the benchmark on LSST precursor data.
AI.motivation: With increasing data volume from surveys like LSST, automated detection of low surface brightness tidal debris and merger signatures is essential for studying galaxy interactions at scale.
AI.method: The authors compare a Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) model (retrained linear classifier only) and the Concentration-Asymmetry-Smoothness (CAS) parameter method (threshold A>0.35) against visual classification as the reference standard for detecting interaction-driven disturbances in galaxies.
AI.result: Visual classification yields 25.1±1.5% disturbance fraction. SSL achieves high recall (0.86±0.04) with low contamination (0.2). CAS shows higher precision (0.77) but much lower recall (0.20). SSL and visual classification show a strong correlation between stellar mass and disturbance fraction, while CAS shows a weaker trend.
AI.conclusion: The SSL model is well-suited for comprehensive detection of merger-related features including faint tidal debris, while the CAS method provides cleaner but incomplete samples; SSL is preferable for a complete census of disturbed systems in large surveys.

title: Towards improved synchrotron self absorption energy estimates: accounting for inhomogeneous and non-spherical emitting regions
summary: Synchrotron self absorption (SSA) is seen across a variety of astrophysical sources, and observation of an SSA peak in the spectrum is a powerful tool for estimating the physical conditions and the minimum energy of the emitting region. We begin with the (re)derivation of the usual SSA parameter estimates, carefully considering dependencies and assumptions, obtaining the most accurate traditional SSA minimum energy equations currently available. Traditional methods rely on the assumption that the emitting region is quasi-spherical and homogeneous. However, many observations of SSA show that the spectral index at frequencies below the peak is less than the expected $+2.5$ (non-thermal) or $+2$ (thermal). We argue that an inhomogeneous emitting region is the most likely explanation in many cases. Power law inhomogeneous cylindrical slab and broken power law inhomogeneous sphere models are used to investigate how the presence of inhomogeneity affects parameter estimates using traditional SSA methods. We find that in some cases inhomogeneity can lead to traditional SSA methods underestimating the minimum energy and the size of the emitting region by over an order of magnitude. Quantitative correction factors are found which can be applied to traditional estimates to correct for inhomogeneity, depending on the value of the observed flattened spectral index and the range in frequency over which this value is observed. Furthermore, we derive simple correction factors for non-spherical homogeneous emitting regions. Finally, we explore the effects of inhomogeneity on measurements of polarisation around the spectral peak, and on lightcurves for expanding emitting regions.

AI.tldr: This paper rederives traditional synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) parameter estimates, identifies that inhomogeneous emitting regions cause spectral flattening (observed spectral index below +2.5/+2), and shows that traditional homogeneous models can underestimate minimum energy and size by over an order of magnitude. Correction factors are provided for inhomogeneous cylindrical slab and broken power-law sphere models, along with corrections for non-spherical geometries and effects on polarization and lightcurves.
AI.motivation: To improve estimates of physical conditions and minimum energy in SSA-emitting regions by addressing the common discrepancy between observed flattened spectral indices below the SSA peak and the predictions of traditional homogeneous models.
AI.method: The authors (re)derive traditional SSA minimum energy equations with careful accounting of assumptions, then develop power-law inhomogeneous cylindrical slab and broken power-law inhomogeneous sphere models. They compare inhomogeneous model predictions to traditional homogeneous estimates and derive quantitative correction factors based on observed flattened spectral index and frequency range.
AI.result: Inhomogeneity can cause traditional SSA methods to underestimate minimum energy and source size by more than an order of magnitude. Correction factors are derived as functions of the observed flattened spectral index and frequency range. Simple corrections for non-spherical homogeneous regions are also provided. Inhomogeneity affects polarization measurements around the spectral peak and lightcurves of expanding sources.
AI.conclusion: Inhomogeneity is the most likely explanation for observed spectral flattening below the SSA peak in many sources. Traditional SSA estimates must be corrected using the provided factors to avoid significant underpredictions of energy and size. The results are broadly applicable across various astrophysical sources exhibiting SSA.

title: Spiral arms across cosmic time: JWST measurements of the pitch angles of spiral galaxies at $z<3.5$
summary: The properties of spiral galaxies in the early universe remain poorly studied and, as such, little is known about their nature and evolution. We use JWST data to measure the pitch angles of spiral galaxies across cosmic time. Our sample consists of 593 spiral galaxies with stellar masses ($M_*$) greater than $10^{10} M_\odot$ up to $z \sim 3.5$, drawn from the CEERS and JADES surveys. Spiral galaxies are identified by fine-tuning a Zoobot deep-learning model. We use SpArcFiRe to identify spiral arms and measure their pitch angles. We find no significant redshift evolution in the average pitch angle across the full sample. However, in the most massive systems (log$(M_*/M_\odot)=11-12$), spiral arms slightly wind up with time. We show that at $z>1.25$, pitch angle does not correlate with some key internal galaxy properties (stellar mass, bulge mass, disk mass, specific star formation rate [sSFR]). In contrast, at $z<1.25$, pitch angle shows a weak but statistically significant negative correlation with stellar mass, bulge mass, and disk mass, and a positive correlation with sSFR at $z<0.75$. We also find no dependence of pitch angle on the tidal strength applied by nearby companions. These results indicate a transition epoch at $z\sim1$: above this redshift, spiral structures appear to be primarily locally driven and not correlated with global galaxy properties; and below this redshift, spiral arms are regulated by global gravitational potential, consistent with the predictions of the density wave theory.

AI.tldr: Using JWST data and machine learning (Zoobot, SpArcFiRe) on 593 massive spiral galaxies up to z~3.5, this study finds no redshift evolution in average pitch angle, but massive systems (log M*/M⊙=11-12) show slight winding over time. Pitch angle correlates with galaxy properties only at z<1.25 (weakly), indicating a transition at z~1 from locally driven to globally regulated spiral structures.
AI.motivation: Spiral galaxies in the early universe are poorly understood; the study aims to quantify their spiral structure (pitch angles) across cosmic time to understand their nature and evolution.
AI.method: 593 spiral galaxies (M*>10^10 M⊙, z<~3.5) from CEERS & JADES surveys; identified via fine-tuned Zoobot deep-learning model; spiral arms and pitch angles measured using SpArcFiRe; correlations with stellar mass, bulge mass, disk mass, sSFR, and tidal strength analyzed at high and low redshift bins.
AI.result: No significant redshift evolution in average pitch angle overall; most massive systems show slight winding over time. At z>1.25, pitch angle does not correlate with internal galaxy properties. At z<1.25, weak negative correlations with stellar/bulge/disk mass and positive with sSFR (z<0.75). No dependence on tidal interactions.
AI.conclusion: A transition epoch at z~1: above this redshift, spiral structures are primarily locally driven (not correlated with global properties); below, they are regulated by global gravitational potential, consistent with density wave theory.

title: Ring Position Angles and Spin in M87* and Sgr A*
comment: Submitted to OJAp (14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table)
summary: Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) images of black holes appear as rings with a brightness asymmetry. Here, we expand on our previous study of the asymmetry magnitude $a_1$ to study the position angle of the peak brightness asymmetry $\mathrm{PA}_1$ in general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) models. For larger spin magnitudes ($a_{*}>0$ and $a_{*}\lesssim-0.5$), the mean $\mathrm{PA}_1$ falls within $1σ$ of the approaching limb of the black hole, regardless of viewing inclination, disk magnetization, or source. By comparing the $(a_1, \mathrm{PA}_1)$ distribution in M87* observations with models, we demonstrate that we can mildly disfavor low-magnitude spins and strongly disfavor all spin vectors that point toward Earth. The alignment of $\mathrm{PA}_1$ relative to the large-scale jet axis may suggest that M87*'s disk does not have a large tilt. By combining $\mathrm{PA}_1$ with the pattern speed measured in optimistic 2026 M87* video conditions, the EHT can constrain whether M87* is prograde or retrograde with $\sim 84\%$ accuracy. In Sgr A*, we show that a detection of $(a_1, \mathrm{PA}_1)$ could constrain the magnitude and direction of the galactic center spin vector. Finally, if future EHT expansions increase the sample of horizon-scale sources, a simple set of observables (ring diameter, asymmetry magnitude, and asymmetry angle) could enable robust constraints on black hole mass, spin, and inclination.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the study of black hole image asymmetry by analyzing the position angle of peak brightness (PA₁) in GRMHD models. It finds PA₁ aligns with the approaching limb for moderate-to-high spins, enabling constraints on M87* spin direction (disfavoring Earth-pointing spins) and suggesting a non-tilted disk. It predicts ~84% accuracy in distinguishing prograde/retrograde M87* spin with 2026 EHT videos, and shows similar analysis can constrain Sgr A* spin. Future EHT expansions could enable mass, spin, and inclination constraints via simple observables.
AI.motivation: To expand previous work on black hole image asymmetry magnitude to include the position angle of peak brightness, enabling better constraints on black hole spin magnitude, direction, and disk orientation from EHT observations.
AI.method: The study analyzes GRMHD simulations across varying black hole spins (a*), viewing inclinations, disk magnetizations, and sources, computing the asymmetry magnitude a₁ and position angle PA₁. These predictions are compared against EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A*, and forecasting is done for future EHT capabilities.
AI.result: For high spin magnitudes (a*>0 and a*≲-0.5), mean PA₁ aligns within 1σ of the approaching limb. Comparison with M87* observations mildly disfavors low spins and strongly disfavors Earth-pointing spin vectors. PA₁ alignment relative to the jet axis suggests minimal disk tilt. Future EHT videos (2026) could distinguish prograde vs. retrograde M87* spin with ~84% accuracy. Similar analysis can constrain Sgr A* spin vector.
AI.conclusion: The position angle of brightness asymmetry is a powerful observable for constraining black hole spin direction and magnitude. Combined with future EHT capabilities, this approach can distinguish spin orientation, probe disk tilt, and with expanded source samples, enable robust constraints on fundamental black hole parameters.

title: Phase-dependent magnetic coherence in the turbulent interstellar medium
summary: Magnetic fields permeate the multiphase interstellar medium (ISM), yet their phase-dependent structure remains poorly constrained by observations. Dust polarization and \ion{H}{1} emission together offer complementary probes of the plane-of-sky magnetic field and cold neutral medium (CNM) gas structure, respectively. Recent observational work has shown that in the diffuse ISM, the dust polarization fraction correlates positively with the CNM mass fraction ($f_{\rm CNM}$) but not with total \ion{H}{1} column density, suggesting a phase-dependent magnetic field geometry. Here, we use extremely high-resolution ($2048^3$) simulations of the turbulent, magnetized, multiphase ISM to investigate the physical origin of this trend. By constructing synthetic \ion{H}{1} and dust polarization maps, we directly compare our simulations to the observational results of \citet{Lei:2024}. We recover a positive $f_{\rm CNM}$-polarization correlation most clearly for sightlines intersecting fewer than $\sim$20 discrete CNM clouds, while the trend becomes weak or intermittent for larger cloud counts, consistent with the expectation that high-Galactic-latitude sightlines contain relatively few independent cold structures. We show that this correlation reflects genuine phase-dependent magnetic structure: CNM clouds tend to be elongated along the local magnetic field and, when normalized by column density, exhibit lower magnetic disorder than the warm neutral medium (WNM). We further demonstrate that apparent discrepancies between simulation- and observation-based measures of magnetic disorder arise from whether disorder is quantified per unit path length or per unit mass. Our results support a picture in which CNM structures host relatively ordered magnetic fields, producing higher polarization fractions along CNM-dominated sightlines in the diffuse ISM.

AI.tldr: Using high-resolution (2048^3) simulations of the multiphase ISM, this study recovers and explains the observed positive correlation between CNM mass fraction and dust polarization fraction, showing it arises from CNM clouds being elongated along the magnetic field with lower magnetic disorder than the WNM, with the correlation strongest for sightlines with fewer than ~20 CNM clouds.
AI.motivation: To investigate the physical origin of the observed correlation between CNM mass fraction and dust polarization fraction in the diffuse ISM, and to understand phase-dependent magnetic field geometry that remains poorly constrained by observations.
AI.method: Used extremely high-resolution (2048^3) simulations of turbulent, magnetized, multiphase ISM; constructed synthetic HI and dust polarization maps; directly compared simulations to observational results; quantified magnetic disorder per path length vs per mass.
AI.result: (1) Positive f_CNM-polarization correlation recovered for sightlines with <~20 CNM clouds; (2) Correlation reflects genuine phase-dependent magnetic structure - CNM clouds elongated along local B-field and exhibit lower magnetic disorder than WNM when normalized by column density; (3) Discrepancies between simulation/observation-based measures of magnetic disorder arise from quantification per path length vs per mass.
AI.conclusion: CNM structures host relatively ordered magnetic fields, producing higher polarization fractions along CNM-dominated sightlines in the diffuse ISM.

title: The Light Curve of Wind-Reprocessed Tidal Disruption Events
summary: The source of the optical/UV emission in tidal disruption events (TDEs) remains an enduring question in the field. Connecting the observed emission to the source is critical for both our understanding of these transients and for using TDEs to study the efficiency of super-Eddington accretion and black hole growth. To explore this connection, we ran time-dependent 1D radiation hydrodynamic simulations of TDE emission with the Sedona monte carlo radiative transfer code, focusing on the reprocessing paradigm. Our simulations follow a compact, evolving X-ray and EUV bright source and surrounding reprocessing outflow over multiple months, using luminosities and mass flow rates consistent with hydro simulations of tidal disruptions. We determine the efficiency of reprocessing as a function of time in this dramatically changing environment and reproduce key observables including timescales, luminosities, and color evolution. Notably, we see a strong wavelength-dependence in the emission timescale due to reprocessing effects. Early on there is an X-ray flare which quickly fades as material builds up and obscures the hot source. At the same time, the optical/UV luminosity begins to rise. Though the optical/UV light curve has a similar shape to the bolometric light curve, the optical peak is offset by $\sim$3 weeks from the bolometric peak due to the time required to build up the reprocessing layer. This implies that early time, high energy emission may be missed for TDEs discovered in optical surveys, and the initial disruption and mass return time to the black hole may occur earlier than optical light curves suggest.

AI.tldr: Using 1D radiation hydrodynamic simulations with the Sedona Monte Carlo code, the authors show that reprocessing by an outflow causes optical/UV emission to peak ~3 weeks after the bolometric (X-ray) peak in tidal disruption events, explaining why early high-energy emission may be missed in optical surveys.
AI.motivation: To understand the source of optical/UV emission in TDEs and connect observed emission to physical processes, which is critical for understanding super-Eddington accretion and black hole growth.
AI.method: Time-dependent 1D radiation hydrodynamic simulations using the Sedona Monte Carlo radiative transfer code, modeling a compact X-ray/EUV source surrounded by a reprocessing outflow over multiple months with luminosities and mass flow rates from hydro simulations of tidal disruptions.
AI.result: Strong wavelength-dependent emission timescale due to reprocessing: an early X-ray flare quickly fades as material builds up, while optical/UV luminosity rises ~3 weeks after the bolometric peak, offsetting the optical peak from the bolometric peak.
AI.conclusion: Early high-energy emission may be missed in optical surveys; the initial disruption and mass return to the black hole likely occur earlier than optical light curves suggest.

title: Morphology, sizes, and scatter in a large sample of distant quiescent galaxies
summary: After quenching galaxies keep growing in size across time, as established in the literature up to cosmic noon. In this work, we assemble one of the largest and most comprehensive multi-wavelength photometric sample of massive quenched galaxies at z > 3, counting 137 quiescent candidates within 825 sq.arcmin and redshift 3<z<7 across the well-studied extragalactic JWST fields. We model their surface brightness distribution across 5 bands mapping their UV-to-NIR rest-frame wavelength with Sersic profiles, and derive their sizes, concentrations, and ellipticities. The size-mass relation is consistent with previous studies. Size decreases with increasing redshift, in agreement with previous studies and extending them up to z_spec=4.9. The intrinsic scatter of the mass-size relation has no relevant dependence on the redshift and the filter used. Our multi-wavelength modeling reveals that size decreases with increasing observed wavelength, and the wavelength gradient decreases with increasing stellar mass. This result proves that in the NIR-bands massive elliptical galaxies appear more compact. The Sersic index does not show significant dependence on wavelength, independently of the stellar mass. Following a forward/backward Bayesian fit analysis to assess the significance of several parameters in predicting the size of our sample, we do not identify any significant secondary dependence of the size on axis ratio q, Sersic index n, UVJ-colors, and environment. The combination of stellar mass and redshift is sufficient to predict the size of quiescent galaxies at z>3, albeit with a large scatter. This suggests that the commonly used parameters of a Sersic distribution cannot explain the large intrinsic scatter around the stellar mass-size relation, suggesting that other physical quantities need to be taken into account to break the degeneracy between evolution paths across the galaxy population.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes 137 massive quenched galaxies at z>3 using JWST data, finding that their size decreases with increasing redshift and observed wavelength, with the stellar mass-size relation showing no strong secondary dependence on morphology, color, or environment, but exhibiting large intrinsic scatter that cannot be explained by standard Sérsic parameters.
AI.motivation: To understand how quenched galaxies evolve in size at high redshift (z>3) and to investigate what physical parameters drive the scatter in the mass-size relation beyond redshift and stellar mass.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength Sérsic profile fitting across 5 UV-to-NIR rest-frame bands for 137 quiescent galaxy candidates in JWST extragalactic fields (825 sq.arcmin, 3<z<7), combined with Bayesian forward/backward fitting to assess secondary parameter dependencies.
AI.result: Size decreases with increasing redshift (up to z_spec=4.9) and with increasing observed wavelength; wavelength gradient decreases with increasing stellar mass; Sérsic index shows no significant wavelength dependence; no significant secondary dependence of size on axis ratio, Sérsic index, UVJ colors, or environment; large intrinsic scatter remains in the mass-size relation.
AI.conclusion: Stellar mass and redshift alone are sufficient to predict quiescent galaxy sizes at z>3, but the large intrinsic scatter suggests that standard Sérsic parameters cannot break the degeneracy between evolution paths, implying other physical quantities are needed to fully understand galaxy size evolution.

title: Long thermonuclear burst driven thermal-viscous instability of accretion disk: triggering an outburst-like X-ray flare
summary: We report on NICER and MAXI observations of a long-duration thermonuclear X-ray burst and a subsequent outburst-like X-ray flare from the neutron star low-mass X-ray binary MAXI J0911--655. Prior to the burst, the source was in a persistent low/hard state with a power-law-dominated spectrum ($Γ\sim 1.7$) and a mass accretion rate of $\sim 1\%$ of the Eddington limit. The long burst, detected by MAXI on 2020 May 22 (MJD 58991.7101), was rapidly followed up by NICER. From time-resolved spectroscopy of the cooling tail, we estimate an exponential decay time of $\approx43$ minutes, the ignition column depth of $\approx0.1\times 10^{12}~{\rm g ~cm^{-2}}$, the burst fluence of $\approx 1.1\times 10^{-4}~{\rm erg~cm^{-2}}$, and the total energy release of $\approx1.2\times10^{42}$ erg. Approximately one day after the burst onset, the 0.5-10 keV light curve unexpectedly re-brightened, initiating an outburst-like flare. During the peak of this flare, the persistent power-law flux increased from its pre-burst level of $\sim0.27\times10^{-9}~{\rm erg~cm^{-2}~s^{-1}}$ to $1.4\times10^{-9}~{\rm erg~cm^{-2}~s^{-1}}$. This flux enhancement was accompanied by significant spectral softening, with the photon index increasing to $Γ\sim 2.2$. Subsequently, the flux decayed and the source returned to its baseline low/hard state. The observed timescales and energetics suggest that intense irradiation from the long burst amplified the ongoing thermal-viscous accretion process. This heating drove an inside-out heating front that temporarily enhanced the mass accretion rate, providing compelling observational evidence of a thermonuclear burst directly modulating the accretion dynamics of its surrounding disk.

AI.tldr: NICER and MAXI observations of a long-duration thermonuclear X-ray burst from MAXI J0911-655 revealed a ~43 min cooling tail, ~0.1×10¹² g cm⁻² ignition column, and ~1.2×10⁴² erg total energy. A day later, an outburst-like flare occurred with flux increasing from 0.27×10⁻⁹ to 1.4×10⁻⁹ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹ and spectral softening (Γ from 1.7 to 2.2), providing evidence that thermonuclear bursts can modulate the surrounding accretion disk via irradiation-driven heating fronts.
AI.motivation: To investigate the interaction between thermonuclear X-ray bursts and the accretion disk in neutron star low-mass X-ray binaries, specifically testing whether burst irradiation can dynamically alter the mass accretion rate and disk structure.
AI.method: Time-resolved spectroscopy of the NICER and MAXI data during the long-duration thermonuclear burst cooling tail and the subsequent flare; spectral fitting of power-law models to track photon index (Γ) and flux evolution.
AI.result: The burst had an exponential decay time of ~43 min, ignition column ~0.1×10¹² g cm⁻², fluence ~1.1×10⁻⁴ erg cm⁻², and total energy ~1.2×10⁴² erg. The delayed flare showed a 5-fold flux increase (from 0.27×10⁻⁹ to 1.4×10⁻⁹ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹) and spectral softening (Γ from ~1.7 to ~2.2), followed by a return to baseline.
AI.conclusion: The observations provide compelling evidence that intense irradiation from a long-duration thermonuclear burst can amplify thermal-viscous accretion, driving an inside-out heating front that temporarily enhances the mass accretion rate — directly demonstrating that thermonuclear bursts can modulate the accretion dynamics of the surrounding disk.

title: CRIRES+ reveals the chemistry of the stellar sub-populations in the bulge fossil fragment Liller 1
comment: Accepted for publication on ApJ, 16 pages, 11 figures
summary: In this paper we present the chemical screening of the complex stellar population discovered in the Bulge Fossil Fragment Liller 1. This study is part of the Bulge Cluster Origin (BulCO) survey based on a Large Program at the ESO-VLT with the high resolution spectrograph CRIRES+. The survey is aimed at performing an unprecedented chemical screening of 17 stellar systems orbiting the Milky Way bulge, with the ultimate goal of unveiling their origin and true nature. We measured precise chemical abundances of iron, CNO, iron-peak, $α$- other light-elements, and neutron-capture elements for a sample of 30 red giant branch stars, kinematic members of Liller 1. The presented analysis provides the high-resolution spectroscopic proof of the complex chemistry of this massive stellar system, with multi-metallicity sub-populations of different ages that nicely fits into a self-enrichment scenario. We find no evidence for the Na-O anticorrelation associated with genuine globular clusters; rather the overall abundance trends are similar to those seen in the bulge field and in Terzan 5, providing definitive evidence of an in-situ formation of Liller 1 within the Galactic bulge.

AI.tldr: This paper presents chemical abundance measurements of 30 red giant stars in Liller 1, a Bulge Fossil Fragment, using CRIRES+ spectroscopy. The analysis reveals multi-metallicity sub-populations, no Na-O anticorrelation, and abundance patterns similar to the Galactic bulge and Terzan 5, supporting an in-situ formation within the bulge.
AI.motivation: To unveil the origin and true nature of Liller 1 and other stellar systems orbiting the Milky Way bulge through a comprehensive chemical screening as part of the Bulge Cluster Origin (BulCO) survey.
AI.method: High-resolution spectroscopy with CRIRES+ at ESO-VLT to measure precise chemical abundances of iron, CNO, iron-peak, α-elements, other light elements, and neutron-capture elements for 30 red giant branch stars that are kinematic members of Liller 1.
AI.result: Confirmed complex chemistry with multi-metallicity sub-populations of different ages; no Na-O anticorrelation (characteristic of genuine globular clusters) was found; abundance trends resemble those of the bulge field and Terzan 5.
AI.conclusion: The chemical evidence supports a self-enrichment scenario and provides definitive proof of in-situ formation of Liller 1 within the Galactic bulge, classifying it as a Bulge Fossil Fragment rather than a genuine globular cluster.

title: An Exploration of Recombination of Uranium with application to Kilonovae Spectra
summary: Dielectronic recombination (DR) is expected to be the dominant recombination process during the non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) phase of kilonovae, yet reliable DR data remain unavailable for most heavy ions. Current spectral models therefore rely on simplified recombination prescriptions, introducing significant uncertainties into predicted spectra. We present an optimization strategy for open f-shell ions using \texttt{AUTOSTRUCTURE}, targeting uranium ions U II--U IV relevant to kilonova ejecta. As a benchmark case, calculations are performed for Nd III to validate the treatment of the f-shell structure and its impact on DR. The resulting DR rate coefficients are of order $10^{-10}$--$10^{-12}$ cm$^{3}$s$^{-1}$ over temperatures relevant to kilonova plasmas. The optimized rates are intended for implementation in radiative-transfer calculations with \texttt{SUMO} to assess the sensitivity of kilonova spectra to improved recombination physics. The Nd III benchmark demonstrates that refinements to the atomic structure can produce measurable changes in spectral features, motivating similar calculations for actinide ions.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an optimization strategy for dielectronic recombination (DR) rate coefficients in open f-shell ions using AUTOSTRUCTURE, targeting U II–U IV for kilonova modeling, with Nd III as a benchmark validating the approach. DR rates (~10⁻¹⁰–10⁻¹² cm³s⁻¹) are derived for kilonova temperatures, and the work aims to improve radiative-transfer calculations via SUMO.
AI.motivation: Reliable dielectronic recombination (DR) data are unavailable for most heavy ions in kilonova plasmas, and current spectral models rely on simplified recombination prescriptions that introduce significant uncertainties into predicted spectra.
AI.method: An optimization strategy for open f-shell ions is developed using AUTOSTRUCTURE, targeting U II–U IV. Nd III is used as a benchmark to validate the treatment of f-shell structure and its impact on DR rate coefficients.
AI.result: DR rate coefficients are of order 10⁻¹⁰–10⁻¹² cm³s⁻¹ over kilonova-relevant temperatures. The Nd III benchmark demonstrates that refinements to atomic structure produce measurable changes in spectral features.
AI.conclusion: The optimized DR rates are intended for implementation in SUMO radiative-transfer calculations to assess spectral sensitivity to improved recombination physics, motivating similar calculations for actinide ions.

title: JADES: the mass-metallicity relation at $z=1-10$. New calibrations, extremely metal-poor galaxies, and chemical diversity
summary: We present gas-phase metallicities of star-forming galaxies at $z=1$-10 with deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra from the JADES full data release, Dark Horse, and OASIS programmes. We stack $\sim$1500 medium-resolution spectra, yielding detections of the [OIII]$λ$4363 auroral line down to $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=7.0$ to derive stack-based strong-line calibrations over the metallicity range $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=7.0$-8.7. At a fixed metallicity, our stacks exhibit [OIII]$λ$5007/H$β$ and [OIII]$λ$5007/[OII]$λλ$3726,3729 values generally lower than calibrations based on high-$z$ individual auroral-line emitters, suggesting an observational bias towards higher excitation introduced when requiring auroral line detections in individual spectra. Based on our new calibrations, we obtain canonical mass-metallicity relations (MZRs) at z$=$1-10, identifying a decrease in metallicities from $z\sim0$ to z$\sim$4-10, without significant change in slope. Moreover, we identify 50 promising candidates of extremely metal-poor galaxies (EMPGs) with $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=6.7$-7.3 (1-4\% solar metallicity) at $z=1.2$-9.1. The MZRs of EMPGs are characterised by a large scatter, with those having lower metallicities generally exhibiting lower sSFRs, opposite of what expected from the local Fundamental Metallicity Relation. These results support a stochastic star-formation history involving gas consumption/ejection and metal-poor inflow, strongly affecting metallicities of low-mass galaxies. Furthermore, we identify two Little Red Dots in our EMPG candidates, both exhibiting broad H$α$ and prominent Ly$α$, offering insights into the early black-hole growth in extremely metal-poor environments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents gas-phase metallicities of star-forming galaxies at z=1-10 using deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra. By stacking ~1500 medium-resolution spectra, the authors derive strong-line calibrations down to 12+log(O/H)=7.0, find observational bias in auroral-line detections, establish mass-metallicity relations, identify 50 extremely metal-poor galaxies (EMPGs), and discover two Little Red Dots with broad Hα and Lyα emission in EMPG candidates.
AI.motivation: To derive robust metallicity calibrations across a wide redshift and metallicity range using deep JWST/NIRSpec spectra and to characterize the mass-metallicity relations and extremely metal-poor galaxies at high redshift.
AI.method: Stacking of ~1500 medium-resolution JWST/NIRSpec spectra from JADES, Dark Horse, and OASIS programmes; detection of [OIII]λ4363 auroral line down to 12+log(O/H)=7.0 to derive strong-line calibrations; analysis of mass-metallicity relations and search for extremely metal-poor galaxies.
AI.result: Stack-based strong-line calibrations show lower [OIII]λ5007/Hβ and [OIII]λ5007/[OII] values at fixed metallicity vs. individual auroral-line emitters, revealing observational bias. Mass-metallicity relations show decreasing metallicities from z~0 to z~4-10 with stable slope. Fifty EMPG candidates identified at z=1.2-9.1 (1-4% solar). EMPGs show large scatter in MZR with lower-metallicity ones having lower sSFR, opposite of local FMR. Two Little Red Dots found among EMPG candidates.
AI.conclusion: Observational bias exists in auroral-line selected samples. Stochastic star-formation with gas consumption/ejection and metal-poor inflow strongly affects metallicities of low-mass galaxies. Early black-hole growth occurs in extremely metal-poor environments.

title: Centrifugal instability of compressible flows and the hydrodynamic stability of accretion disks
summary: A recent analysis of the centrifugal instability in the case of pressure-supported compressible relativistic rotation, with application to astrophysical jets, yielded a generalisation of the famous Rayleigh criterion for Newtonian flows. According to this criterion, the centrifugal instability is strongly affected by the flow Mach number, and not only in the relativistic fluid dynamics but also in its Newtonian limit. To validate the Newtonian version of this criterion, we performed axisymmetric numerical simulations of non-relativistic transonic rotating flows which are stable according to the original Rayleigh criterion but can be either stable or unstable according to the new one. The results of computer simulations are found to be in perfect agreement with the theory. The hydrodynamic stability of accretion disks is often explained by referring to the original Rayleigh criterion, even if their rotation is highly supersonic. To clarify the matter, we analysed the hydrodynamic stability of flows rotating about central compact object and derived an instability criterion that retains the explicit dependence on the flow Mach number. This criterion turns out to be equivalent to the standard Solberg-Høiland criterion, which does not involve the Mach number. The same applies to the case of pressure-supported rotation, where the role of gravity is played by the centrifugal force.

AI.tldr: This paper validates a generalized Rayleigh criterion for centrifugal instability in rotating flows, showing that the Mach number affects stability in both relativistic and Newtonian regimes. Numerical simulations confirm the theory, and the criterion is shown to be equivalent to the standard Solberg-Høiland criterion when applied to accretion disk hydrodynamics.
AI.motivation: To validate a generalized Rayleigh criterion for centrifugal instability that accounts for Mach number dependence, and to clarify the role of this criterion in hydrodynamic stability of accretion disks where rotation is often highly supersonic.
AI.method: Axisymmetric numerical simulations of non-relativistic transonic rotating flows that are stable under the original Rayleigh criterion but can be either stable or unstable under the new generalized criterion.
AI.result: Numerical simulations perfectly agree with the generalized theoretical criterion. The new Mach-number-dependent criterion is shown to be equivalent to the standard Solberg-Høiland criterion, which does not explicitly involve Mach number.
AI.conclusion: The Mach number affects centrifugal instability criteria in both relativistic and Newtonian limits, but the generalized criterion reduces to the standard Solberg-Høiland criterion for pressure-supported rotation, resolving the apparent discrepancy.

title: Imprints of the Neutral Interstellar Medium on Polarized Synchrotron Emission and Faraday Rotation
summary: The interstellar medium (ISM) is a complex, multiphase medium, where disentangling the distribution of gas and magnetic field structure across different phases remains a considerable challenge. Recently, Faraday tomography enabled by broadband polarized radio observations has emerged as a promising probe of 3D ISM gas and magnetic field structures. However, the interpretation of these observations is obscured by our limited understanding of the different ISM components probed by the distinct Faraday depth features. In this work, we present a comprehensive multi-frequency ($\sim$300 MHz - 23 GHz) analysis comparing features in the Faraday-rotated, polarized synchrotron emission and HI structures over the full high-latitude (|b|>30 degrees) diffuse sky. Using measures of HI structure complexity along the line of sight (LOS), we observe enhanced depolarization across synchrotron radio frequencies in regions with high HI complexity characterized by multiple HI velocity components. We also find that the first and second moments of the Faraday depth spectra are linked to the underlying neutral gas structure. These results indicate that regions of the ISM that are dominated by neutral gas could directly contribute a significant portion of the diffuse synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation. These findings establish new observational constraints for Galactic magnetic field models that synthesize multiphase tracers into a single coherent picture.

AI.tldr: The study presents a multi-frequency analysis (300 MHz–23 GHz) comparing Faraday-rotated polarized synchrotron emission with HI structures across the high-latitude diffuse sky, finding that regions with complex HI velocity structure show enhanced depolarization and that Faraday depth spectrum moments link to neutral gas structure, suggesting neutral gas contributes significantly to diffuse synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation.
AI.motivation: The interstellar medium (ISM) is a complex multiphase medium where disentangling gas distribution and magnetic field structure across different phases remains challenging; Faraday tomography's potential is limited by our poor understanding of which ISM components produce distinct Faraday depth features.
AI.method: A comprehensive multi-frequency analysis (≈300 MHz–23 GHz) comparing Faraday-rotated polarized synchrotron emission with HI structure complexity measures over the full high-latitude (|b|>30°) diffuse sky, using HI velocity components to characterize line-of-sight complexity.
AI.result: Enhanced depolarization is observed in regions with high HI complexity (multiple velocity components); first and second moments of Faraday depth spectra are linked to underlying neutral gas structure.
AI.conclusion: Regions dominated by neutral gas could directly contribute significant portions of diffuse synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation, establishing new observational constraints for Galactic magnetic field models that synthesize multiphase tracers.

title: A Jet from a Nearly Dormant Black Hole
summary: Most galaxies host supermassive black holes (SMBHs) that remain weakly accreting or dormant for much of their lifetimes. At the lowest accretion rates, these systems may represent the transition between active nuclei and dormant black holes, but whether they can still launch collimated jets remains unclear. The nuclei in our Galaxy (\sgra) and M31 are key examples of this regime, although no clear jet structure has yet been detected in either source. Here we report multi-frequency very long baseline interferometric observations of \Msixty\ (NGC~4649), a nearby elliptical galaxy hosting a nearly dormant SMBH with an Eddington ratio of $\sim10^{-8}$. We detect a compact two-sided jet with an unusually steep synchrotron spectrum, demonstrating that collimated outflows can persist even under nearly dormant accretion conditions. The apparent radio core exhibits an unprecedentedly steep frequency-dependent position shift toward the SMBH, locating the central engine only $\sim57\,μ$as, corresponding to a projected distance of $\sim10$ Schwarzschild radii, upstream of the 8.37-GHz core. The observed jet morphology and steep core-shift behaviour are reproduced by general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic and radiative-transfer simulations, indicating a magnetically dominated, non-equipartition jet-launching region that departs from the standard conical equipartition picture. These results provide direct observational evidence that jet production can survive near the dormant SMBHs and establish \Msixty\ as a unique laboratory for probing jet formation on event-horizon scales in the lowest-accretion SMBH regime.

AI.tldr: This paper reports VLBI observations of M60 (NGC 4649), a dormant SMBH with an Eddington ratio of ~10⁻⁸, detecting a compact two-sided jet with a steep synchrotron spectrum and an unprecedentedly steep core-shift toward the SMBH, demonstrating that collimated jets can persist under nearly dormant accretion conditions.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether collimated jets can be launched from SMBHs at extremely low accretion rates (Eddington ratio ~10⁻⁸), representing the transition between active nuclei and dormant black holes.
AI.method: Multi-frequency very long baseline interferometric (VLBI) observations of M60 (NGC 4649) combined with general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) and radiative-transfer simulations.
AI.result: Detection of a compact two-sided jet with unusually steep synchrotron spectrum; observation of an unprecedentedly steep frequency-dependent core-shift toward the SMBH, locating the central engine ~57 μas (~10 Schwarzschild radii) upstream of the 8.37-GHz core.
AI.conclusion: Jet production can survive near dormant SMBHs, and M60 serves as a unique laboratory for probing jet formation on event-horizon scales in the lowest-accretion SMBH regime, with the launching region being magnetically dominated and departing from the standard conical equipartition picture.

title: Flagging Super-Eddington Candidates among Jetted, γ-Ray-Emitting AGN
comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, submitted as a proceedings paper to Physical Science Forum
summary: The quasar Eigenvector-1/Main Sequence (E1/MS) provides a physically motivated empirical framework to organize the spectroscopic diversity of type~1 active galactic nuclei (AGN). In its optical plane, the full width at half maximum of H$β$ and the Fe\,II strength ratio $R_{\mathrm{FeII}}$ define a sequence that is primarily driven by Eddington ratio, with important secondary roles played by black-hole mass, orientation, spectral energy distribution, and chemical enrichment. The E1/MS framework is therefore well suited to identify highly accreting and possibly super-Eddington (SE) sources, usually associated with the extreme Population~A (xA) spectral types. We discuss why E1/MS is a useful tool to search for SE accretors among jetted AGN and, conversely, to place $γ$-ray-detected AGN in the broader context of quasar phenomenology. We summarize two complementary results: (1) some candidate SE accretors show radio properties such as high brightness temperature non-thermal cores or radio lobes} consistent with jet activity; and (2) a subset of low-redshift $γ$-ray narrow-line Seyfert~1 galaxies exhibit optical spectra consistent with xA or borderline-xA classification. We also expand the discussion of recent developments in E1/MS studies, including metallicity trends, the spectral energy distribution of xA quasars, and the role of highly accreting quasars as discovery tools for extreme accretion states, as probes of quasars at the reionization epoch, and as possible cosmological probes.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses how the quasar Eigenvector-1/Main Sequence (E1/MS) framework, defined by Hβ line width and Fe II strength, organizes type 1 AGN spectroscopic diversity and identifies super-Eddington accretors. It explores connections between extreme Population A sources and jetted/γ-ray AGN, and reviews recent developments including metallicity trends, SED properties, and the use of highly accreting quasars as probes for extreme accretion, reionization-era studies, and cosmology.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the utility of the Eigenvector-1/Main Sequence framework for identifying super-Eddington accreting sources among jetted and γ-ray-detected AGN, and to expand the discussion of recent developments in E1/MS studies.
AI.method: Synthesis and discussion of empirical E1/MS optical plane (Hβ FWHM vs. R_FeII) as a diagnostic for Eddington ratio, black-hole mass, orientation, SED, and chemical enrichment; analysis of radio and γ-ray properties of extreme Population A (xA) spectral types.
AI.result: (1) Candidate SE accretors show radio signatures of jet activity (e.g., high brightness temperature non-thermal cores, radio lobes). (2) Some low-redshift γ-ray narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies have optical spectra consistent with xA or borderline-xA classification.
AI.conclusion: The E1/MS framework is a powerful tool for identifying super-Eddington accretors among jetted AGN and for contextualizing γ-ray AGN within quasar phenomenology. Highly accreting quasars serve as valuable probes for extreme accretion physics, reionization-epoch studies, and cosmological applications.

title: Spectral study of X-ray sources in some galaxies recently observed by Chandra
comment: Published in Indian Journal of Physics
summary: With the aim to study the spectral properties of some X-ray sources from recently observed {\it Chandra} data, 9 galaxies which have been observed by {\it Chandra} ACIS-S during the year 2018 to 2022 have been considered for the present work. 27 sources with net source counts $ \ge$ 100 have been considered. The spectra of all the sources were fitted using two empirical models -- an absorbed powerlaw and an absorbed disk blackbody. From their estimated bolometric luminosities, the 27 X-ray sources are categorized as 6 X-ray binaries (XRBs) and 21 Ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs). All the six XRBs are found to be in the spectrally hard state ($Γ\sim$ 1.52-2.29) which indeed may be due to thermal comptonization. Only one ULX, CXOUJ032251.2-370950 (X-5), was found to be spectrally soft while the remaining 20 ULXs were spectrally hard. The spectral parameters of X-5 with an inner disk temperature (kT$_{in}$) $\sim $ 0.5 keV and an estimated bolometric luminosity, L$_X \sim$ 3.26 $\times$ 10$^{39}$ erg s$^{-1} $ requires a black hole of mass, M$_{BH} \sim$ 137.86$^{+66.62}_{-47.41}$ M$_\odot $ accreting at $ \sim$ 0.19 times its Eddington limit. 8 ULXs, X-4, X-8, X-9, X-10, X-11, X-12, X-20 and X-21, were found to be in the Extremely luminous X-ray sources (ELXs) regime with even their lower limit of luminosity $>$ 10$^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$. Softening/Hardening of spectra with or without changes in the luminosity were also observed in some ULXs/ELXs. In the hard ELX, X-8, spectral softening with almost consistent luminosity was observed. While in the ULXs X-20 and X-25 spectral softening with increasing luminosity was observed. However spectral hardening with increase in luminosity were observed in the ULXs X-21 and X-26.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes 27 X-ray sources from 9 galaxies observed by Chandra (2018-2022), categorizing them into 6 X-ray binaries (XRBs) and 21 ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs) based on bolometric luminosities. All XRBs are in a spectrally hard state. Among ULXs, one (CXOUJ032251.2-370950) is spectrally soft, implying a ~138 M☉ black hole accreting at ~0.19 Eddington; 8 ULXs enter the extremely luminous X-ray source (ELX) regime. Varied spectral softening/hardening with luminosity changes are observed across sources.
AI.motivation: To study the spectral properties of X-ray sources from recently observed Chandra data, specifically to categorize and understand the physical nature (XRBs vs. ULXs) and accretion states of these sources based on spectral modeling.
AI.method: Selected 27 sources with net counts ≥100 from 9 galaxies observed by Chandra ACIS-S (2018–2022). Fitted spectra using two empirical models: an absorbed powerlaw and an absorbed disk blackbody. Classified sources via estimated bolometric luminosities.
AI.result: 6 XRBs (all spectrally hard, Γ~1.52–2.29); 21 ULXs (1 soft, 20 hard). The soft ULX (X-5) has kT_in~0.5 keV, L_X~3.26×10³⁹ erg/s, implying M_BH~138 M☉ at ~0.19 Eddington. 8 ULXs are in the ELX regime (L>10⁴⁰ erg/s). Spectral softening/hardening with or without luminosity changes observed.
AI.conclusion: The sample reveals a dominance of spectrally hard ULXs, one notable soft ULX implying an intermediate-mass black hole candidate, and a subset of ELXs. Spectral variability patterns (softening/hardening with luminosity) suggest diverse accretion regimes in these extragalactic X-ray sources.

title: SDSS-V LVM: Revealing the Physical and Chemical Structure of the Helix Nebula
summary: We present the first spatially contiguous study of the physical and chemical structure of the Helix Nebula (NGC~7293, PNG 036.1-57.1) based on integral-field spectroscopy from the SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM). The wide-field observations provide nearly complete spectroscopic coverage of the nebula, enabling a spaxel-by-spaxel analysis of extinction, electron density and temperature, ionisation structure, and chemical abundances. We reconstruct calibrated datacubes from the LVM row-stacked spectra and measure 41 optical emission lines, including hydrogen, helium, and collisionally excited metal lines. The resulting maps reveal a strongly stratified nebula, with highly ionised gas traced by \heii~concentrated toward the central cavity, low-ionisation material dominating the bright shell, and neutral or transition-zone gas enhanced in the outer regions. The Helix is a low-density object, with typical electron densities of $\sim10^{2}\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, and exhibits a non-uniform temperature structure, with variations of several thousand Kelvin across different ionisation zones. We derive a near-solar oxygen abundance, $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})\simeq8.7$, consistent with spatially complete sampling. The central abundance pattern indicates a significant contribution from unobserved O$^{3+}$, suggesting that apparent abundance variations are primarily driven by ionisation effects rather than true chemical inhomogeneities. We also find evidence for a sulfur deficit of $\sim$1 dex, consistent with the planetary-nebula sulfur anomaly. The helium and nitrogen abundances place the Helix near the classical boundary of Type~I planetary nebulae, suggesting moderate chemical enrichment by its progenitor star.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first spatially contiguous integral-field spectroscopic study of the Helix Nebula using SDSS-V LVM data, analyzing extinction, electron density/temperature, ionization structure, and chemical abundances across the entire nebula, revealing strong stratification, low density (~10² cm⁻³), near-solar oxygen abundance, a sulfur deficit (~1 dex), and moderate chemical enrichment consistent with a borderline Type I planetary nebula.
AI.motivation: To provide the first complete spatially contiguous study of the physical and chemical structure of the Helix Nebula (NGC 7293) using integral-field spectroscopy from SDSS-V LVM, enabling spaxel-by-spaxel analysis that overcomes limitations of previous slit-based or narrowband studies.
AI.method: Integral-field spectroscopy from SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM); reconstruction of calibrated datacubes from row-stacked spectra; measurement of 41 optical emission lines (H, He, collisionally excited metal lines); spaxel-by-spaxel mapping of extinction, electron density (e.g., [S II] doublet), electron temperature ([O III], [N II], [S II]), ionization structure, and chemical abundances.
AI.result: Revealed a strongly stratified nebula: He II concentrated in central cavity, low-ionization gas in bright shell, neutral/transition-zone gas in outer regions. Low density (~10² cm⁻³). Non-uniform temperature structure with variations of several thousand K. Near-solar oxygen abundance (12+log(O/H)~8.7). Central O³⁺ contributions indicate apparent abundance variations are ionization-driven. Sulfur deficit ~1 dex (PN sulfur anomaly). He and N abundances place Helix near classical Type I PN boundary.
AI.conclusion: The Helix Nebula shows strong ionization stratification, low density, and non-uniform temperature. Chemical abundances are consistent with near-solar metallicity, with ionization effects driving apparent abundance variations. The sulfur anomaly is confirmed. The progenitor star produced moderate chemical enrichment, placing the nebula at the Type I PN boundary.

title: Gamma-Ray Constraints on Heavy Axion-Like-Particle Decays from Fermi-LAT and H.E.S.S. Blazar Spectra
comment: 27 pages, 9 figures, Prepared for submission to JCAP
summary: The propagation of very-high-energy (VHE; $E_γ \geq 100$ GeV) gamma rays from extragalactic sources is affected by interactions with photons of the extragalactic background light (EBL), resulting in pair production that attenuates the intrinsic gamma-ray flux. This interaction renders the Universe increasingly opaque to VHE photons at high energies and redshifts. New physics scenarios involving axion-like particles (ALPs) could modify this expected optical depth. In particular, ALPs with masses $m_a \sim 10$ eV can decay into two photons over cosmological timescales, thereby contributing to the diffuse EBL. If such ALPs constitute a significant fraction of the dark matter density, their decay would enhance the EBL intensity and consequently increase the gamma-ray optical depth. In this study, we investigate this scenario using a large sample of gamma-ray spectra observed with the High Energy Stereoscopic System (H.E.S.S.) and the Fermi Large Area Telescope. We model the contribution of decaying ALPs to the EBL and assess their impact on the spectra of blazars across redshifts. By comparing these observations with standard EBL models, we place constraints on the properties of heavy ALPs, specifically their mass and photon coupling, and evaluate their viability as a dark matter candidate capable of modifying the gamma-ray transparency of the Universe. From the combined analysis, and under the assumption that ALPs constitute the entire dark matter density, we derive 95% confidence exclusion limits on the photon-ALP coupling down to $g_{aγ} \sim 7 \times 10^{-12}$ GeV$^{-1}$ for masses $m_a\sim 15$ eV. These constraints are competitive with existing astrophysical bounds and provide complementary sensitivity to other techniques, closing a previously unconstrained region of parameter space in the $m_a \sim 2.5$-$20$ eV range.

AI.tldr: This paper uses H.E.S.S. and Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations of blazars to constrain axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses ~10 eV that decay into photons, contributing to the extragalactic background light and increasing gamma-ray opacity. The analysis excludes photon-ALP couplings down to ~7×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ at 95% confidence for ALPs constituting all dark matter, closing previously unconstrained parameter space in the 2.5–20 eV mass range.
AI.motivation: Very-high-energy gamma rays from extragalactic sources are attenuated by pair production with extragalactic background light (EBL) photons. Axion-like particles (ALPs) decaying into two photons could contribute to the EBL, modifying gamma-ray opacity. If ALPs constitute dark matter, their decay would enhance the EBL and increase the optical depth for gamma rays, providing a testable signature.
AI.method: The authors model the contribution of decaying ALPs (masses ~10 eV) to the EBL spectrum and predict the resulting impact on gamma-ray optical depth. They compare a large sample of blazar spectra observed with H.E.S.S. and Fermi-LAT against standard EBL models, fitting for ALP parameters (mass and photon coupling) under the assumption that ALPs constitute the entire dark matter density.
AI.result: From the combined analysis, the authors derive 95% confidence exclusion limits on the photon-ALP coupling down to g_{aγ} ~ 7×10⁻¹² GeV⁻¹ for masses m_a ~ 15 eV. These constraints are competitive with existing astrophysical bounds and close a previously unconstrained region in the m_a ~ 2.5–20 eV range.
AI.conclusion: Heavy ALPs decaying to photons can be constrained via their contribution to the EBL and consequent modification of gamma-ray transparency. The derived limits are competitive with other methods and close an unconstrained parameter region, demonstrating the power of gamma-ray observations to probe ALP dark matter scenarios.

title: Investigating the role of turbulence in the interstellar medium in $z\sim3$ dusty star-forming galaxies using kpc-resolution ALMA dust and gas maps
summary: We present ALMA high-resolution ($\sim$0.25$^{\prime\prime}$/2 kpc) CO(5-4) and CO(4-3) observations of three $z\sim 3$ submillimetre-selected dusty galaxies from the ALESS survey. These data complement existing [sub]-kpc scale ALMA 870$μ$m continuum imaging and JWST NIRCam and MIRI imaging from the ALESS-JWST program, allowing us to trace the molecular gas, dust-obscured star formation, and stellar populations on similar spatial scales. We spectroscopically confirm that two of the sources lie at the same redshift and are likely interacting. We find that the molecular-gas distribution broadly follows the dusty star-forming structures seen in the 870$μ$m dust continuum imaging, but that the gas reservoirs are significantly more extended than the dust emission with a spatial extent comparable to the rest-frame near-infrared stellar emission. By modeling the kinematics for the two highest signal-to-noise sources, we find that the galaxies are well-fit by rotating disc models with high ratios of ordered to random motion ($V_{\rm{max}}/\overlineσ=5\pm1$ and $6\pm1$), although smaller-scale kinematic deviations cannot be ruled out at the current sensitivity and spatial resolution. Finally, utilizing the high-resolution 870$μ$m dust continuum and CO data, we investigate star-formation scaling relations on kpc-scales in these high-redshift galaxies. Assuming a constant CO-to-H$_{2}$ conversion factor and excitation ratio, we find that the data are offset from theoretical star-formation relation predictions that do not take turbulence into account, but consistent with gravo-turbulent models, thereby suggesting that turbulence plays a central role in regulating star formation at high redshift.

AI.tldr: This study presents ALMA CO(5-4) and CO(4-3) observations of three z~3 dusty galaxies from the ALESS survey, revealing that molecular gas extends more than dust emission, the galaxies are likely interacting rotating discs with high ordered-to-random motion, and the kpc-scale star-formation relations favor gravo-turbulent models over non-turbulent predictions, highlighting turbulence's role in regulating high-redshift star formation.
AI.motivation: To complement existing sub-kpc ALMA 870μm and JWST imaging, enabling multi-phase (molecular gas, dust-obscured star formation, stellar populations) spatial analysis of high-redshift dusty galaxies.
AI.method: High-resolution (~0.25″/2 kpc) ALMA CO(5-4) and CO(4-3) observations of three z~3 ALESS submillimeter galaxies, combined with existing 870μm continuum and JWST NIRCam/MIRI data. Kinematic modeling (rotating disc fits) and kpc-scale star-formation scaling relation analysis.
AI.result: Two sources are at the same redshift and likely interacting. Molecular gas is more extended than 870μm dust emission, comparable to rest-frame near-IR stellar emission. Best-fit rotating disc models yield V_max/σ̄ = 5±1 and 6±1. CO-based SFR relations are offset from non-turbulent theoretical predictions but consistent with gravo-turbulent models.
AI.conclusion: Turbulence plays a central role in regulating star formation in high-redshift galaxies.

title: Detection of a parsec-scale, compact, and fading ejecta from an accreting massive black hole
summary: Dwarf galaxies, characterized by their low luminosities and masses, are excellent candidates for searches for intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs), particularly when they show strong accretion and ejection activity. The dwarf galaxy SDSS J101747.09+393207.7 has recently been found to display a very high X-ray luminosity and an X-shaped optical structure, possibly caused by a dwarf--dwarf merger. To explore its potential IMBH ejection activity, we performed very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) observations at 4.9 GHz. In this work, we present the detection of a milliarcsecond-scale, compact, sub-microjansky radio component near the optical centroid. According to some existing radio sky survey data, the radio component was not detected until 2015; it displayed an optically thin steep radio spectrum and declining flux densities across 0.8--5 GHz from 2019 to 2025.
